subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve gearing increased after weeks two/three for higher travel speed.
subsystems.intake: Everybot-derived rollers grip the cone rim; wrist flip supports acquisition from either cone direction.
subsystems.transfer: Direct acquisition; protective side guards deploy alongside the exposed mechanism.
subsystems.scoring: Lifter accepts target positions; wrist and lift motion overlap.
subsystems.endgame: Not established in the retrieved interview.
subsystems.controls: Time-of-flight sensors measure piece offset inside the wide gripper; camera alignment compensates for that offset.

versions: Original guards also tipped cones; redundant front portion removed. Wrist motion overlapped with lift. Separate autonomous cone slammer added for faster preload scoring.
dossier.analysis: Especially useful for two interacting costs: a wide gripper reduces pickup alignment but introduces unknown piece offset; sensing resolves that offset before placement. Impact protection is treated as architecture.
limits: Interview configuration and reported revisions are documented; full season chronology remains to be audited against the linked releases.

context_documents.title: 2023-1756 · Deployable bash guards protect a collector but can obstruct scoring
context_documents.body:
# 2023-1756: Deployable bash guards protect a collector but can obstruct scoring

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

An Everybot-style roller gripper and flipping wrist acquire cones from either direction. Deployable side bash guards move with the exposed collector. Lift and wrist motion overlap to reduce delay, while driver modes control guard behavior.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly says preventing damage is preferable to repeatedly replacing the collector. It also notes that guards should not deploy during scoring because they would contact the wall.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A protective structure changes the collision envelope it is intended to manage. It can improve floor acquisition under defense while creating a new field-contact risk near the grid. The safe state therefore includes the guards, not only the arm and gripper. Overlapped motions save time only if their intermediate envelopes remain clear.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test lateral collector impacts, scoring-wall clearance and interrupted transitions. Measure full pickup-to-release time with the guard interlocks active.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/EVxz7j82Cp4](https://youtu.be/EVxz7j82Cp4)

source_reviews.title: Argos 2023 Judge Handout
source_reviews.locator: PDF p. 2, drivetrain, intake/placer, arm, controls and bash guards
source_reviews.review_basis: Read text of the team's handout via its season archive.
source_reviews.facts: Describes the ball-screw shoulder actuator, perforated tube rack, integrated flipping head, paired guards and homing strategy.
source_reviews.limitations: The handout describes intended functions and does not date configuration changes.

source_reviews.title: Argos 2023 robot code
source_reviews.review_basis: Read command and subsystem implementation in public checkout.
source_reviews.facts: Profiles combine shoulder, extension and guard motion. Wrist flips are gated by extension. Piece detection uses distance and stator current, and guard homing has a failure path.
source_reviews.limitations: Competition and practice settings coexist. The snapshot does not identify which build ran in a particular match.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Argos carried one intake/placer on a swerve-mounted telescoping arm. Shoulder angle, telescoping reach and wrist orientation position the piece. Two sliding guards protect the head in exposed poses when enabled, adding a separate axis to the clearance problem. The team paired presets on a dedicated operator panel with kinematic motion generation, so a scoring request represents a coordinated mechanism move.
source_review.piece_flow: The dual roller rows engage the cone at its flange. Cubes are controlled between the lower compliant wheels and the aluminum tube, which also stiffens the head. The piece stays in the intake as the arm travels. The wrist can rotate beyond 180 degrees for cone presentation. The software has separate cone and cube intake and eject routines. Its detection logic combines a piece-specific time-of-flight result with absolute stator current above 7 A. Cone distances also feed a filtered position estimate.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The pivoting member houses a tube-in-tube extension, and the wrist needs swing clearance near the chassis. In the command implementation, selected poses include a bash-guard target. An arm waypoint path is profiled with a keep-out polygon, and its profiles are combined with a separately generated guard profile. During travel the wrist can start moving when extension and other command conditions permit. Inference: the programmed clearance has to cover the deflected, loaded mechanism and the game piece, especially following an impact or a homing offset.

subsystems.name: Shoulder and extension
subsystems.construction: Ball-screw linear actuator with custom gearbox raises the arm. Sprocket teeth engage a CNC-routed hole pattern in a nested tube as a modified rack and pinion.
subsystems.operation: The shoulder moves the inner tube's line of action, while extension sets radial reach. Position requests are converted to coordinated shoulder and extension motion.
subsystems.team_rationale: Argos documents configurable conversion from sensor readings to physical units and preset movement through a kinematic model.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Actuator leverage changes through the pivot arc. A perforated rack also concentrates load at the hole edges. Test both for play and tracking in loaded reversals.
subsystems.interfaces: The shoulder pivot transmits reach and piece loads to the chassis. The extending tube carries wrist, rollers and their harness.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect actuator pivots, hole wear and tube guides. Verify virtual retract reference after changing guide fit or disassembling the transmission.
subsystems.unknowns: Actuator force curve, sprocket geometry and tube-guide stack.

subsystems.name: Wrist and roller head
subsystems.construction: Dual axles with compliant wheels, rigid aluminum tube and a powered flipping wrist.
subsystems.operation: The intake controls the piece while it changes orientation. The pose command distinguishes roller-up and roller-down targets and restricts early flips to a defined arm envelope.
subsystems.team_rationale: The integrated head serves both acquisition and placement. LEDs communicate intent and intake status.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Cone flange engagement and cube compression impose different contact requirements. A current spike can also come from an obstruction, so evaluate it together with distance and retention.
subsystems.interfaces: Wrist and intake wiring follow the extending arm. The pose command reads piece orientation when selecting an end attitude.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check time-of-flight range with dirty sensors and crushed or skewed pieces. Validate reverse and interrupted wrist transitions with an actual piece.
subsystems.unknowns: Roller durometers, speed, field-side release accuracy and sensor false-positive rates.

subsystems.name: Bash guards and chassis
subsystems.construction: Paired guard tubes driven by a sprocket and hex shaft. Guards tilt downward and the drivetrain is swerve.
subsystems.operation: Guard deployment is operator-selectable. The subsystem has soft limits after homing, and pose command initialization can exclude guard motion when guard home has failed.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team wanted extra intake protection and specified a downward deployment angle to keep the guards in the bumper zone.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Guard contact can redirect load into the chassis and a bent tube may consume clearance even when encoder position reads correctly.
subsystems.interfaces: Guard targets are included in the arm motion command. Chassis pose determines clearance to the grid and field structures.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: After side contact, check both tubes for unequal travel and rehome. Exercise the homing-failure branch before relying on degraded operation.
subsystems.unknowns: Guard material, impact ratings, exact event fit and measured scoring-wall clearance.

revisions: The archived code contains competition and practice hardware definitions. No dated sequence of mechanical guard or arm revisions was established.
transferable_principles: Treat protection hardware as a moving subsystem with explicit targets, homing and collision checks. Use both geometric and load signals when the same roller contact must identify two different pieces.
disconfirming_conditions: If guard travel consumes grid clearance or repeated side impacts prevent retraction, deployment trades collector damage for cycle failures. If flange orientation varies beyond wrist and jaw tolerance, integrated pickup requires more driver alignment.
remaining_gaps: Quantified arm and guard clearances, exact stage and wiring service procedures, event revision chronology and timed pickup-to-placement distributions.
